Read with HANDOFF_vignettes_release_0.4.1_2026-10-28.md (references, rulings, task-doc lessons, where things live — all still hold) and its _v2 (vignette state and the release plan, of which §1 and §3 are superseded below). Written by chat at the close of the efficiency-routes chat (2026-10-28/29), from the CC reports of that chat and the GitHub master read read-only.

2. Release-content freeze — what the vignette chat may and may not touch before 10 November

  • In the CRAN tarball (any change re-opens the release: the final check must be re-run on the release branch and cran-comments.md re-stated): vignettes/forestsearch.qmd, R/, man/, DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, NEWS.md, README.md, inst/, tests/. Treat these as frozen for 0.4.1 unless a defect is found; if the primary vignette must change before the 10th, the change goes on release/0.4.1 (or on master before the release merge, followed by a re-merge) and ends with the one as-cran check.
  • Not in the tarball (.Rbuildignore: ^vignettes/articles$, ^_pkgdown\.yml$, ^docs$, ^quarto$, ^dev$, ^HANDOFF_.*\.md$): the pkgdown articles, _pkgdown.yml, the quarto documents, dev records, handoffs. Article revisions can proceed on a feature branch now and merge any time; they reach the site through the pkgdown workflow on master and never touch the submission. Standing rules for them are in the pkgdown-articles notes: .qmd, based on the CRAN release, small simulation counts with the “real applications run 5,000–10,000” note, rendered HTML kept locally and never staged by a task.
  • Vignette/article items carried over, none blocking: the primary vignette’s “about a minute and a half on one core” against a measured 1:14 (cosmetic; in the tarball, so it waits for the next release unless the release branch is reopened anyway); the .gitignore decision for vignettes/articles/*.html (forestsearch-2024.html tracked, three renders untracked and not ignored); the ACTG175 GLM article follows the release; the v1 handoff §6 items 2–11.

3. The efficiency question — closed for 0.4.1 (decision memo decision_efficiency_routes_0.4.1_2026-10-28.md, chat-side; the project KB was out of room)

  • Re-based on the post-lean replicate (lean-fits Stage C: survival 2.02 s, continuous 1.84 s, binary 2.75 s), the deferred consistency-stage items are B+H 20.4% (survival), E+H 10.9% (continuous), G+H 8.0% (binary) — all below the 30% bar; C (multicore) 2.6–8%; D (chunking) ≤ 14.6%; medians 5–6% (declined 09-02). High confidence: direct-timer method, which predicted A and F to within 0.07 s.
  • Recorded, not proposed: B+H could clear only on a campaign shape with ≈ 210+ candidates entering the consistency stage (applications: 120–136) — unmeasured; a zero-R/ one-call measurement under a null/uniform-benefit DGM at c1 0.90 / c2 0.80 / p* 0.90 would settle it, after the release. Search-stage bookkeeping (ceilings 19–30%, realizable share unmeasured, touches enumeration order — not for a patch release). MR inference is outside the survey’s scope and is, by subtraction, most of the vignette’s 74 s and of the application documents.
  • Lesson kept: if B/E/G/H are ever done, do them as one “consistency pieces on vectors” refactor sharing the lean cores, not four items.

5. Open items after the release (recorded; a task only when Larry commissions)

  1. The consistency-stage pieces (.consistency_glm_pieces(), R/consistency_resample.R) take no weights for any ps_adjust_method: an IPTW analysis is weighted in the search stage and unweighted in the consistency screen (binary OR too). A method question.
  2. At is.RCT = FALSE with defaults (ps_method = "grf", ps_adjust_method = "none") a propensity forest is fitted per call and per bootstrap replicate and never consumed, and the rebuilt estimator closure is untagged (lean path lost). Also a stale design comment was corrected (forestsearch_main.R PS block: default is "none").
  3. subgroup_glm() (R/run_subgroup_sims.R) routes only the continuous case to a fast closure; one constructor shared with forestsearch() would close the drift (no committed consumer).
  4. With use_lasso = TRUE under a null DGM, replicates where LASSO selects a single covariate end in get_FSdata: no candidate cut expressions … returning NULL result (seen in the old run_null_calibration example; caught by the function; invisible in the fixed-family configuration). Looks like a defect of the LASSO-screened path when exactly one variable survives.
  5. The campaign-shape measurement of §3 (B+H).
  6. Hard-coded 1.96 in the GLM search-stage CI vs qnorm(0.975) on the Cox path; fixed 95% — a flexibility note; changing it moves displayed GLM bounds at the 4th digit.
  7. .gitignore for vignettes/articles/*.html; the primary vignette’s “minute and a half” sentence; v1 handoff §6 items 2–11.

6. Protocol clarifications from this chat (apply going forward)

  • Check policy, refined (Larry, 2026-10-29): the concern was needless repetition, not CC running checks. CC runs no check mid-task or per edit; the full R CMD check --as-cran is the last gate of any branch touching R/ (once, before Larry merges) and of the release task, and may be run by CC. Interim verification stays with the task’s own acceptance tests and machine-checkable post-conditions.
  • Closing-block greps must exclude comment lines and string literals (CC’s open item (d) after three self-inflicted mismatches in the robustness task); never count a pattern the task document itself told CC to write into a comment or a message.
  • R CMD check on a plain shell needs pandoc on PATH — now installed; RSTUDIO_PANDOC alone leaves the README/NEWS NOTE.
  • CC stopping at a wrong-branch / unmerged-base gate and reporting is correct behaviour; the fix is Larry’s merge, then re-issue.
  • A measurement stage (Stage A on the unmodified tree, installed first) is the baseline for any R/-touching task; identity is saved-against-saved, component by component, Stage C vs Stage A, with the committed earlier records compared informationally.
  • Behaviour-invariance claims are stated in the task document’s category block and proven in the report from the evidence, never asserted from description.

8. Protocol carried forward

Three layers: Larry decides and approves · chat writes specs and task documents · Claude Code does all repo operations. Task documents travel ~/Downloads → dev/tasks/, committed first and alone; kickoffs short, inline, fenced, the absolute final content of a delivery; “clear CC first, then paste” with every kickoff. Nothing points CC at project-KB paths. Any task touching R/ is called out as moves code / changes behaviour / changes method. Gates stop the task; they do not stop to ask. Compute is a separate go/no-go with wall-clock stated from a measured record. Verify from source, never from description. Findings go in the record; a task is proposed only when something blocks or Larry commissions it. Larry pushes via GitHub Desktop; CC never pushes or merges. Committed work is not re-run or re-verified. Text after > or ❯ in a transcript is CC, not Larry.
